action: Scan the Right Upper Quadrant to locate landmarks.
interpretation: Identify the liver and the diaphragm.

action: Scan more posterior to target the retroperitoneal space. Establish a long or coronal orientation of the right kidney.
interpretation: Visualize the right kidney in the long axis. Recall that kidneys are retroperitoneal structures.
Visualize the capsule of the kidney, noting that it is hyperechoic.

action: Inspect the center of the kidney. Evaluate the echogenicity of the collecting system.
interpretation: Visualize that the center of the kidney is hyperechoic. Interpret this as a collapsed collecting system, indicating no hydronephrosis.

action: Fan the probe through the entire volume of the kidney.
interpretation: Ensure full visualization of the organ to avoid missing pathology.

action: Hold the view on a suspicious area within the kidney.
interpretation: Note a potential tiny area suggestive of a hydro ureter.
Differentiate between mild hydronephrosis/hydro ureter and vasculature.

action: Observe the color flow signals in the suspicious area.
interpretation: Confirm the structures are vessels due to the presence of flow. Rule out hydro ureter. Conclude the kidney is normal.

action: Rotate the probe 90 degrees counterclockwise. Orient the probe marker down towards the bed.
interpretation: Visualize the kidney in a transverse view.
Recognize rib shadowing obscuring the middle of the kidney view.

action: Slide the probe into the intercostal space between ribs. Fan through the kidney to optimize the transverse view.
interpretation: Obtain a clearer transverse view by avoiding the rib shadow.

action: Inspect the center of the kidney in the transverse plane.
interpretation: Verify there is no anechoic area in the center, as an anechoic center would suggest hydronephrosis.
Visualize a hyperechoic white center to confirm the kidney is normal.
